data.title: GEYOTO Wraps Up RE+ 2026 Debut with Strong Visitor Engagement and Real-World Product Experiences
data.description:
GEYOTO Wraps Up RE+ 2026 Debut with Strong Visitor Engagement and Real-World Product Experiences

GEYOTO Wraps Up RE+ 2026 Debut with Strong Visitor Engagement and Real-World Product Experiences

PR Newswire

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026

From creator coverage and product demonstrations to an artist-painted N1000, GEYOTO's Las Vegas debut connected energy innovation with everyday needs.

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GEYOTO concluded its first appearance at RE+ 2026 with an active booth, interest among content creators and visitors, and product experiences that brought its "Go-to Energy" philosophy to life. During the Nov. 17–19 exhibition at the Las Vegas Convention Center, attendees stopped to photograph the booth, explore new products and speak with the team about energy needs at home and outdoors.

A First Appearance That Gave Visitors a Reason to Stop

At Booth C4753, sandstone textures and warm desert tones gave GEYOTO an American Southwest-inspired setting. The oversized "YO!" installation at the front added a playful welcome, expressing the brand's lively, approachable personality and giving visitors another reason to stop and take a photo.

Content creators, including @911Reviews and @Minute Man Solar, visited the booth to explore and record the new lineup. Alongside invited creators, other attendees passing through the exhibition also stopped to film and photograph the products, drawn to their distinctive designs. Attendees shared their own photos and posts on social media, carrying their impressions of GEYOTO beyond the exhibition floor.

This interest also led to conversations with distributors, retailers and solar industry professionals about product applications and potential North American partnerships, giving the team opportunities to continue discussions beyond the show.

Product Stories That Went Beyond the Specification Sheet

The N1500X demonstration setup was one of the booth's focal points, inviting visitors to look more closely at the model's outdoor-oriented protective design. With an IP65 rating for dust and water resistance, the portable power station gave the team a concrete starting point for discussing outdoor use, product protection and practical operating needs.

Another memorable exhibit was an N1000 previously used by participants at Burning Man and featuring original artwork painted by several artists. Brought from the desert to RE+, the unit paired a real-world use story with a distinctive visual identity, showing how a power station can support outdoor experiences while becoming part of the memories people bring home.

New Products Built Around Practical Details

GEYOTO's next-generation N300L, N1000L and N2000L portable power stations put a familiar travel inconvenience in focus: managing charging cables. Each model features an integrated retractable cable that delivers up to 140W of fast charging to compatible devices, bringing cable storage and device charging together in one design.

On the solar side, the S200 Rigid and S400 Rigid panels use heterojunction (HJT) cell technology and support bifacial generation, with a bifaciality rating of up to 95%. Reinforced aluminum frames are designed to support long-term outdoor use. The modular Y3000 and Y6000 balcony energy storage systems added another application to the display, with battery expansion options for different energy needs.

Small Gestures Made Energy Useful on the Show Floor

Beyond the displays, the team offered hats, charging adapters and cables, along with access to charging at the booth. For visitors who needed to recharge a device during the show, GEYOTO's products became part of their day rather than simply something to look at.

For some visitors, interest went beyond filming and conversation. Several visitors asked to buy the equipment directly and take it home, and nearly all of the spare units available at the booth were purchased on site. The response gave GEYOTO a tangible sign of product appeal during its first RE+ appearance.

As RE+ 2026 came to a close, GEYOTO left with new industry contacts, content from creators and attendees, and direct feedback from people who had seen and used its products. From a charging cable offered when a visitor needed one to a power station taken home after the show, the debut connected GEYOTO's products with real people and immediate needs, giving its "Go-to Energy" philosophy a practical expression.

Reliable Energy Ready for Real Life.

About GEYOTO

GEYOTO develops portable power stations, solar panels and modular balcony energy storage systems, focusing on reliable energy solutions designed around everyday needs.

Website: https://www.geyoto.com/

Columbia Seligman Premium Technology Growth Fund Announces a Special Fourth Quarter Distribution

Today, Columbia Seligman Premium Technology Growth Fund, Inc. (NYSE: STK) (the Fund) declared a special fourth quarter distribution, that is beyond its typical quarterly managed distribution policy, in the amount of $13.2298 per share. A federal excise tax of 4% applies to funds that do not distribute substantially all of their annual income (including net gains) before the end of their fiscal year. The Fund’s income for the 2026 fiscal year exceeds the amounts previously distributed pursuant to the Fund’s quarterly managed distribution policy. The Fund is distributing this excess income so that it will not incur the 4% federal excise tax in 2026.

The distribution will be paid on December 22, 2026 (the Payment Date) to stockholders of record on December 2, 2026 (the Record Date). The ex-dividend date is December 23, 2026. Because all of the distribution is expected to be a special capital gain distribution, it will automatically be paid in stock except that any Record Date stockholder may elect to receive the distribution in cash by contacting, as applicable, their financial advisor (for shareholders who hold shares through a financial intermediary, such as a broker-dealer) or the Fund’s stockholder servicing agent, Equiniti Trust Company, LLC, whose contact information appears below (for shareholders who hold shares directly with the Fund), by 5 pm Eastern Time on December 16, 2026. It is anticipated that the Fund will make its next distribution under its managed distribution policy in the month of February.

Because the payment of the special dividend represents more than 25% of the market price per share of the Company’s common shares, the New York Stock Exchange has advised the Company that its common shares will trade with “due bills” representing an assignment of the right to receive the special dividend from the record date of December 2, 2026 through the closing of trading on NYSE on December 22, 2026, which is the payment date and the last day of trading before the December 23, 2026 ex-dividend date (this period of time representing the “Dividend Right Period”).

Shareholders who sell their common shares during the Dividend Right Period will be selling their right to the special dividend, and such shareholders will not be entitled to receive the special dividend. Due bills obligate a seller of common shares to deliver the special dividend payable on such common shares to the buyer (the “Dividend Right”). The record date of December 2, 2026 will be used as the date for establishing the due bill tracking of the Dividend Right to the holder of common shares.

Due bill obligations are customarily settled between the brokers representing the buyers and the sellers of shares. The Company has no obligation for either the amount of the due bill or the processing of the due bill. Buyers and sellers of the Company’s common shares should consult their brokers before trading to be sure they understand the effect of NYSE’s due bill procedures.

data.title: GE HealthCare Foundation announces 2026 grants to expand maternal and pediatric care in underserved communities
data.description:
GE HealthCare Foundation announces 2026 grants to expand maternal and pediatric care in underserved communities

Funding will support organizations across three continents, strengthening clinical training, early detection, surgical care and referral pathways to expand access to lifesaving care

The GE HealthCare Foundation today announced its 2026 cohort of grant recipients, supporting organizations whose work will help expand access to lifesaving care for mothers and children around the world. This year's grantees are focused on building sustainable, technology-enabled healthcare infrastructure, equipping frontline healthcare workers with point-of-care diagnostics and advanced surgical training.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120084087/en/

Healthcare professionals take part in cesarean section training in Nakuru County, Kenya. Through its investment in Global Surgery Foundation’s SURGfund, the GE HealthCare Foundation is supporting locally led efforts to strengthen surgical capacity and expand access to safer surgical care. Photo by Frank Kimaro.

Spanning three continents, these investments reflect the Foundation’s ongoing commitment to improving maternal and pediatric health by strengthening locally led healthcare systems, equipping community-based providers, and building networks that connect mothers and children with lifesaving care. Together, these initiatives aim to address critical gaps in care while building sustainable healthcare capacity in underserved communities.

“True access to quality care is determined by measurable patient outcomes and the long-term resilience of local systems,” said John Schaeffler, President at GE HealthCare Foundation. “By supporting organizations that expand access to diagnostic capabilities and clinical mentorship, the Foundation seeks to help local healthcare teams identify high-risk conditions earlier and make complex procedures safer.”

The work of these grantees impacts communities ranging from the remote Amazon region to underserved rural clinics in Africa. In Brazil, where congenital heart disease drives 6 percent of infant mortality, the funding expands access to early screening to ensure newborns receive timely, life-saving cardiac interventions each year. In Africa, the expansion of clinical training will transition specialized diagnostic imaging directly to local healthcare workers, establishing permanent, high-quality point-of-care ultrasound services for women. Based on projections provided by the 2026 grant recipients, the GE HealthCare Foundation estimates that these grants collectively have the potential to reach approximately 160,000 patients.

The 2026 grant recipients include:

  • The Global Surgery Foundation (GSF) works with local partners to expand access to surgical care for the five billion people in the world currently lacking it. This grant will contribute directly to active projects across India, Nepal, Tanzania, Rwanda, Nigeria, and Kenya. Approximately 920 healthcare workers will be trained with the funding, impacting thousands of patients annually. By building multidisciplinary surgical teams (obstetricians, anesthetists, and midwives) who undergo rigorous simulation-based training, the program aims to deliver documented reductions in surgical complications and significantly improve the safety of cesarean sections.
  • One Economy Foundation is a social welfare organization that exists to bridge the socioeconomic divide by increasing access to prenatal care. The funding will deploy clinic-based and mobile outreach platforms to scale access to early ultrasounds and specialized OBGYN support. Expanding outreach into Namibia, this grant targets young and first-time mothers. The work aims to accelerate the early detection of high-risk pregnancies, improve clinical skills among frontline workers, and guide mothers through an integrated parenting framework.
  • Worldwide Radiology strengthens access to quality diagnostic imaging in underserved areas, working with local health care professionals in Ghana. With this grant, the organization aims to tackle maternal care gaps by certifying 48 clinicians, growing national trainer capacity to 18, and helping ensure that women gain vital access to high-quality specialist point-of-care ultrasound scans annually.
  • Children’s HeartLink aims to save children’s lives by transforming pediatric heart care in underserved parts of the world. This grant targets severe infant mortality disparities in low-access areas of Brazil’s Amazon region. By training 30 referring clinicians and optimizing screening networks within Brazil’s universal health system, the program aims to impact the care of children born with congenital heart disease, while collaborating with public-health stakeholders to integrate congenital heart disease into maternal and child health plans.

The new grants build on the Foundation's initial partnerships, which have also aimed to strengthen local healthcare systems and community networks by reaching the people who need the most care. Recent highlights from the initial grantees include:

  • Project ECHO: In West Java, Indonesia, early results following the implementation of Project ECHO’s Integrated Antenatal Care program, alongside broader health-system improvements, show encouraging progress. Average monthly maternal deaths attributed to preeclampsia and postpartum hemorrhage declined approximately 66%, from nearly three per month in 2025 to one per month during the first four months of 2026.
  • Lwala Community Alliance: In Kenya, Lwala trained 121 health providers across 38 facilities to provide basic ultrasound services. Since early 2025, more than 6,800 pregnant women have received ultrasounds in Lwala-supported facilities, including 2,700 between April and June 2026—nearly seven times the number screened during the same period last year; the work also helped inform Kenya’s 2025 national obstetric point-of-care ultrasound curriculum.
  • Black Mamas Matter Alliance (BMMA): In the U.S., Black Maternal Health Week 2026, the national campaign founded by BMMA, included 550+ community events hosted by Black-led maternal health organizations nationwide, generated 4.1 million+ content views and 111 million+ in media reach, and connected 2.9 million+ people with maternal health resources.

Through these focused investments, the GE HealthCare Foundation continues to champion evidence-based, technology-enabled healthcare that empower local workforces and establish self-sustaining frameworks for healthier communities worldwide.

About the GE HealthCare Foundation

The GE HealthCare Foundation is a charitable organization, incorporated separately from GE HealthCare, that advances access to precision healthcare by funding organizations that make healthcare more accessible, personal, human and flexible. The GE HealthCare Foundation envisions a world where healthcare has no limits, and is on a mission to help create that world — starting with moms and babies.

FRVO INVESTOR DEADLINE APPROACHING: Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP Reminds Fervo Energy (NASDAQ: FRVO) Investors of Securities Class Action Lawsuit Deadline on January 19, 2027

Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP Securities Litigation Partner James (Josh) Wilson Encourages Investors Who Suffered Losses In Fervo Energy To Contact Him Directly To Discuss Their Options

If you purchased or acquired Fervo Energy Class A common stock pursuant and/or traceable to the registration statement and prospectus (collectively, the “Registration Statement”) issued in connection with the Company’s May 13, 2026 initial public offering (“IPO” or the “Offering”) and would like to discuss your legal rights, call Faruqi & Faruqi partner Josh Wilson directly at 877-247-4292 or 212-983-9330 (Ext. 1310).

[You may also click here for additional information]

Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP, a leading national securities law firm, is investigating potential claims against Fervo Energy Company (“Fervo Energy” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: FRVO) and reminds investors of the January 19, 2027 deadline to seek the role of lead plaintiff in a federal securities class action that has been filed against the Company.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120389830/en/

Faruqi & Faruqi is a leading national securities law firm with offices in New York, Pennsylvania, California and Georgia. The firm has recovered hundreds of millions of dollars for investors since its founding in 1995. See www.faruqilaw.com.

As detailed below, the complaint alleges that the Company and its executives violated federal securities laws by making false and/or misleading statements and/or failing to disclose that: (1) that Fervo's pilot plant was experiencing inconsistent production temperatures and premature thermal decline; (2) that Fervo's EGS operations were experiencing significant injected water loss at a level above the rate the Company's commercial plans required; (3) that Fervo's drilling costs were not declining as represented, including as misleadingly represented given previously published data; (4) that Fervo lacked sufficient transmission capacity to deliver power to its California customers as planned, including the transmission path underlying the Company's approximately 290 MW of rights which was scheduled for retirement before Cape Station Phase II's targeted 2028 COD; and (5) that, as a result of the foregoing, Defendants' positive statements about the Company's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

On October 6, 2026, during market hours, Morpheus Research published a report alleging that "Fervo has failed to disclose existential issues related to inconsistent production temperatures and premature thermal decline, excessive water loss, seismicity-related equipment damage, transmission capacity, and ballooning costs. In some cases, Fervo appears to have presented altered data and made material misstatements to investors, including in its [initial public offering] registration statement filed with the [United States Securities and Exchange Commission]." On this news, Fervo's stock price closed as low as $7.79 per share, a more than 71% decline from the $27 per share IPO price.

The court-appointed lead plaintiff is the investor with the largest financial interest in the relief sought by the class who is adequate and typical of class members who directs and oversees the litigation on behalf of the putative class. Any member of the putative class may move the Court to serve as lead plaintiff through counsel of their choice, or may choose to do nothing and remain an absent class member. Your ability to share in any recovery is not affected by the decision to serve as a lead plaintiff or not.

Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP also encourages anyone with information regarding Fervo Energy’s conduct to contact the firm, including whistleblowers, former employees, shareholders and others.

To learn more about the Fervo Energy class action, go to www.faruqilaw.com/FRVO or call Faruqi & Faruqi partner Josh Wilson directly at 877-247-4292 or 212-983-9330 (Ext. 1310).

Follow us for updates on LinkedIn, on X, or on Facebook.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) for Investors Regarding the Fervo Energy Securities Class Action Lawsuit:

What is the Fervo Energy securities fraud lawsuit about?

The lawsuit alleges that Fervo Energy Company made materially misleading statements and omissions to investors concerning the performance and viability of its enhanced geothermal system ("EGS") operations. Specifically, the complaint alleges that Fervo's pilot plant was experiencing inconsistent production temperatures and premature thermal decline, and that its EGS operations were allegedly losing injected water at rates exceeding what the Company's commercial plans required. The lawsuit further alleges that Fervo's drilling costs were not declining as represented, that the Company lacked sufficient transmission capacity to deliver power to its California customers as planned, and that a key transmission path underlying approximately 290 MW of rights was scheduled for retirement before Cape Station Phase II's targeted 2028 commercial operations date. As a result, the complaint alleges that Defendants' positive statements about Fervo's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and lacked a reasonable basis.

Who may be eligible to participate in the lawsuit?

Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Fervo Energy Company (NASDAQ: FRVO) securities during the Class Period may potentially be eligible to participate in this lawsuit. The Class Period dates are not fully specified in the currently available case information and should be confirmed when final case details are published. Importantly, investors do not need to seek appointment as lead plaintiff in order to participate in the lawsuit or to share in any potential recovery. Eligible investors are encouraged to review the complaint and consult with counsel to assess their potential claims.

What is a lead plaintiff, and how can I seek appointment?

A lead plaintiff is a court-appointed representative who acts on behalf of all class members in directing the litigation, including making key strategic decisions and working closely with counsel. Any investor who purchased Fervo Energy securities during the Class Period and suffered a loss may move the court for appointment as lead plaintiff. The deadline to file a motion seeking lead plaintiff appointment is January 19, 2027. Investors should be aware that they are not required to serve as lead plaintiff in order to be a member of the class or to share in any recovery that may be obtained.

Why should investors contact Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP?

Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP has represented investors in securities litigation for decades and has recovered hundreds of millions of dollars for shareholders. Investors who purchased Fervo Energy securities during the Class Period may contact the firm to discuss their legal rights, potential claims, and the lead plaintiff process at no cost or obligation.

Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP (“SBS”), a national shareholder rights litigation firm, reminds investors of a class action lawsuit against Alibaba Group Holding Limited (“Alibaba” or “the Company”) (NYSE: BABA) for violations of §§10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5 promulgated thereunder by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Shareholders who purchased shares of BABA during the class period listed are encouraged to contact the firm regarding possible lead plaintiff appointments. Appointment as lead plaintiff is not required to partake in any recovery.

DEADLINE: January 19, 2027

If you are a shareholder who suffered a loss, click here to participate.

data.title: Shackelford, McKinley & Norton Strengthens Expertise in Dallas Office
data.description:
Shackelford, McKinley & Norton Strengthens Expertise in Dallas Office

Firm adds to industry-leading aviation, commercial litigation, real estate practices

Shackelford, McKinley & Norton, LLP, announces the addition of partners Chris Andrews, J Bailey and Joe Marcus to its aviation and commercial litigation practices. Also joining the firm is real estate associate Nithin Shakamuri. All join the noted full-service transactional and litigation firm’s Dallas office.

Mr. Andrews joins the firm’s internationally recognized aviation practice with a background in regulatory compliance and aircraft leasing and procurement. He is a former attorney with the Federal Aviation Administration’s Office of the Chief Counsel, where he specialized in advising FAA clients on safety reporting programs and safety management systems. He also was FAA counsel for claims arising from the Tort Claims Act.

A member of the Aviation Lawyers Association, Mr. Andrews is a graduate of Drake University College of Law and holds an LL.M. in international aviation law and policy from the DePaul University College of Law.

Mr. Bailey represents owners, contractors, subcontractors and developers across the life of their residential and commercial construction projects. He has served as first-chair counsel in arbitrations, bench and jury trials, leading trial teams from jury selection through closing arguments.

The University of Oklahoma School of Law graduate also frequently serves in an outside general counsel role for clients, negotiating and drafting construction contracts, assisting with employment matters and advising on business issues.

Mr. Marcus is a litigator with more than a decade of experience representing businesses, including electric utilities and cooperatives, in complex, high-exposure litigation involving commercial and contract disputes, defense of catastrophic personal injury and wrongful death claims, construction and real estate disputes, multi-party lawsuits, easement negotiation and easement disputes.

A graduate of the University of Miami School of Law, Mr. Marcus is admitted to practice in Texas, Florida and Colorado. He is a member of the Electric Cooperative Bar Association.

Mr. Shakamuri works with property owners, developers, investors and businesses across a variety of industries, focusing on commercial real estate, corporate and business matters involving real estate acquisitions and dispositions, commercial leasing, development, financing, and mergers and acquisitions.

He is the co-chair of the Dallas Association of Young Lawyers’ transactional law committee and was a member of its 2025 Leadership Class. He is a Brown Family Philanthropy Fellow with Social Venture Partners Dallas. He earned his J.D. from the University of Oklahoma College of Law and an LL.M. in taxation from the Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law.

About Shackelford, McKinley & Norton, LLP

Shackelford, McKinley & Norton, LLP, is a full-service transactional, litigation, aviation and entertainment law firm with attorneys and offices in Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth and Austin, Texas, and New Orleans.

data.title: Hundreds of Clinicians Share PROTEIN NOW!™ Protein Shots
data.description:
Hundreds of Clinicians Share PROTEIN NOW!™ Protein Shots

Hundreds of Clinicians Share PROTEIN NOW!™ Protein Shots

PR Newswire

MIDDLESEX, N.J., Nov. 20, 2026

PROTEIN NOW!™ earns Clinicians' Choice status on FrontrowMD, where more than 800 clinicians and counting have shared the zero sugar, 21 gram protein shot out of hundreds of product options. No clinicians were compensated.

MIDDLESEX, N.J., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NutraBio® Labs, Inc. today announced that PROTEIN NOW!™, its ready-to-drink liquid protein shot, has earned Clinicians' Choice status on FrontrowMD, an independent, third-party platform where clinicians curate a personalized selection of health products for their patients. More than 800 clinicians, including physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician associates, have added PROTEIN NOW! to their personalized FrontrowMD patient pages as of November 2026, and that number continues to grow.

Clinicians use FrontrowMD, a free platform, to build their own selection of health products, and FrontrowMD digitally tracks and verifies which products they include. Products shared by clinicians on FrontrowMD are recognized with its Clinicians' Choice designation.

"Getting your protein in should be easy, and it should come from a product you can feel good about," said Alex Berrio, Director of Marketing at NutraBio Labs. "Seeing hundreds of clinicians share PROTEIN NOW! gives people one more reason to grab one and go."

PROTEIN NOW! is made for people who know protein matters but struggle to fit it into busy days: commuters, parents, travelers, and the growing number of people on GLP-1 medications looking for protein in smaller, easier-to-consume servings. Each 3.38 fl oz shot delivers 21 grams of protein in just 90 calories and requires no mixing, refrigeration, or preparation.

What clinicians are saying

Two physicians describe what stands out about PROTEIN NOW! in their FrontrowMD reviews.

Dr. Salvador Recio, MD, an internal medicine physician with 35 years in practice, wrote: "A lot of protein drinks come with sugar and calories that people don't want, which is why this protein shot from Protein Now! gets my attention." He added: "Notably, it contains no sugar, no fat, and barely any carbohydrates."

Dr. Katie Novitski, MD, a surgeon with 11 years in practice, wrote: "Protein Now! packs a full serving of protein into a small bottle, so the whole thing goes down in a couple of swallows." She added: "Because it is such a concentrated protein source, a good amount can fit into a very small drink."

†These clinician want to clarify that larger-scale research to support their product claims is still developing. These statements have not been reviewed by the FDA and are not intended to be medical advice.

PROTEIN NOW! is available in Orange Mango, Strawberry Watermelon, and Blueberry Acai at proteinnow.com, nutrabio.com, Amazon, and select specialty retailers. Visit our website to learn more and see the clinicians sharing PROTEIN NOW! protein shots.
